findings.title: Only the pre-advance gate fits the state model; pre-tasks and pre-implementation gates have no defined position or status
findings.description:
The document defines four gate transitions: `pre-slice-plan`, `pre-tasks`, `pre-implementation` and `pre-advance`. The status and insertion-point design only works for `pre-advance`.
- `pending-review` is defined as "tasks complete, review gate configured, no review artifact present".
- The insertion point is "between Priority 5 and Priority 6".
- A `pre-tasks` gate would have to fire when `deriveSliceStatus()` returns `needs-tasks` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:470`). A `pre-implementation` gate would fire between `needs-tasks` and `in-implementation`.
- Neither gate has a status value, an insertion point, or a rationale string.
- Overview and Envisioned State say v1 "implements only the four slice-level transitions". But `pre-slice-plan` is called initiative-level and deferred, so only three slice-level transitions exist.
- None of the three Anticipated Slices builds `pre-tasks` or `pre-implementation`.
- The document either needs a gate model that generalizes (status = "gate pending for transition X"), or it should scope v1 to `pre-advance` and drop the other transitions from the schema.

findings.title: "Lexicographically last filename" is not "most recent", and `review-failed` has no exit path
findings.description:
The naming pattern is `NNN-review.{type}.{slug}.md`, for example `210-review.code.github-copilot-vs-code-ide-support.md`. Everything after the type is a slug, so lexicographic order sorts by slug text, not by time. The claim "most recent by sort order" is false.
- **Stale pass hides a new failure.** Suppose a stale `PASS` review sorts after a newly written `FAIL` review. The `PASS` wins and the gate clears.
- **Failed review can never clear.** If a re-run review after a `FAIL` sorts before the failing file, the slice stays `review-failed` forever, with no code path out.
- **No staleness model.** A review of slice code at commit A still clears the gate after more work lands. The document never says what "reviewed" means relative to the current state.
- **No route out of `review-failed`.** The only route is `recommendation: "blocked"`. A runner such as Amoeba can't tell "blocked on a failed review, run the fixer" from any other blocked state. "Above CF's layer" is not enough if the consumer has nothing to branch on.
- **Fix:** select by frontmatter date (`dateCreated`/`dateUpdated`) or mtime, and define what happens with several artifacts.

findings.title: `deriveSliceStatus()` swallows errors, which defeats the "must not silently pass" guarantee
findings.description:
`deriveSliceStatus()` wraps all of its logic in `try { … } catch { return base; }` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:462-496`), and `base.status` is `'no-active-slice'`. The architecture puts review detection and verdict parsing into this method. Any thrown error from reading the review directory, parsing frontmatter, or loading gate config then yields `no-active-slice`. `getNext()` Priority 2 turns that into "You have a slice plan but no active slice. Pick your first slice" (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:98-166`). That is a wrong, silent recommendation, and it contradicts both "treated as UNKNOWN" and the project rule against silent fallbacks.
The document does not say how config errors are surfaced. `NextAction` has only `warnings`, with no error channel. The review-read path needs its own non-throwing result type, or the existing catch needs narrowing. The document should say which.

findings.title: The recommendation "vocabulary" the gate promises doesn't exist, and "no 160 interfaces change" is false
findings.description:
Related Work says Amoeba "depends on CF returning structured `recommendation` values with a stable vocabulary" and that 240 "is purely additive; no 160 interfaces change".
- **Free-form prose, not an enum.** `NextAction.recommendation` is `string` (`types.ts:281`). Every existing value is prose, such as "Advance to slice N: name" and "Continue implementation — 3 tasks remaining". A bare `"review"` or `"blocked"` is a one-off token inside a prose channel. Consumers must string-match.
- **No machine-readable discriminator.** The Design Goals claim runners can "act on them without parsing recommendation strings", but `NextAction` carries no status or kind field. Slice status lives on `WorkflowStatus.activeSlice`, not on `NextAction`. A discriminator such as `kind` or `gate` is needed on `NextAction`. Without it the stated goal isn't met.
- **Closed unions change.** `SliceStatus.status` is a closed union (`types.ts:257`) and `DocumentDetectionResult` gains a field. Adding union members is a breaking change for exhaustive consumers: `buildSummary()`, the MCP schemas, and anything keyed on `'complete'`. `complete` also now means something different, since a slice whose tasks are done may report `pending-review`.
- **Missing consumer inventory.** The document needs an inventory of those consumers.

findings.title: Verdict, threshold and unknown-policy semantics are inconsistent
findings.description:
- **Misnamed value.** The config block lists threshold `"concerns"` and unknown policy `"fail"`. Technical Considerations then uses `review_unknown_as = "concern"` (singular). The allowed value sets are never enumerated.
- **Undocumented `pending` outcome.** The `pending-review` definition says UNKNOWN can be "treated as pending" by `review_unknown_as`. Verdict handling lists no such value, only fail-like and concern-like behavior.
- **Undefined ordering.** "`CONCERNS` clears if `review_threshold = "concerns"` or lower" implies an ordering of threshold values that isn't defined. What would `"fail"` mean as a threshold? It would clear everything, including `FAIL`.
- **Unspecified matching.** Config uses lowercase (`pass`, `concerns`) and verdicts uppercase. Frontmatter matching is not specified as case-insensitive. The project rules on lenient parsing mean `verdict: pass` shouldn't become UNKNOWN.
- **Contradictory goal.** The Design Goals line says the default "blocks on `FAIL` or `UNKNOWN`", but UNKNOWN is policy-dependent.
- **Two dimensions.** Verdict (3 values plus UNKNOWN) times threshold times unknown-policy gives an interaction matrix that should be one table, not prose.

findings.title: The config surface is under-specified and conflicts with the Fail-fast principle
findings.description:
- **Contradiction.** The Fail-fast principle says per-gate config errors are caught by "the `validate` hook in `ConfigKeyDefinition`". The actual interface (`ConfigKeys.ts:1-7`) only supports scalar `type`, `enum` and `validate(value)`. The `validate` signature doesn't receive the key. Technical Considerations admits nested tables aren't modeled and defers the decision to "slice design time".
- **Wrong slice order.** That decision determines the shape of the first Anticipated Slice, which adds "per-gate override structure to `ConfigKeys.ts`".
- **Missing defaults.** `reviewType` has no default. If a user sets only `review_enabled = true`, it's unclear what is gated: nothing, or `pre-advance` with an unspecified type. "No gate configured → advance" implies nothing, which makes the global threshold key nearly meaningless alone. The project rule bans silent defaults.
- **Unspecified worktree scope.** Related Work says the keys "should be resolvable at worktree scope". Nothing says how `WorkflowNavigator` obtains resolved config today, or how a nested table merges across scopes.
- **Prefer `enum`.** Use the existing `enum` field for threshold and policy values instead of custom `validate`.

findings.title: The ConsistencyChecker rule conflicts with the gate and is likely to produce noise
findings.description:
- **Different notions of "complete".** The Navigator gate operates on the active slice and "complete" means all task checkboxes are checked. The checker rule operates on slices "marked complete in the slice plan". This is a different source of truth, and it covers every completed slice, not just the active one.
- **Historic noise.** Flipping `review_enabled = true` on an existing project would emit warnings or errors for every historical slice, including ones with legacy review files lacking `verdict` (they become UNKNOWN, then fail by default).
- **Duplicated logic risk.** The gate logic lands in the Navigator in slice 2 and an independent rule lands in the checker in slice 3. There is no shared component (for example a `ReviewGateEvaluator`) that both call. Verdict-versus-threshold logic would be written twice, against the DRY rule.
- **Severity mismatch.** A missing review is a `warning` in the checker but a hard stop in the Navigator.

findings.title: The Squadron slice 300 contract is a load-bearing dependency with no pinned shape
findings.description:
CF's whole v1 depends on a `verdict` key from an external initiative's contract. The document does not state:
- whether `verdict` is a top-level key,
- its allowed casing,
- whether slice 300 has landed,
- or the set of valid `reviewType` values (`arch`/`slice`/`tasks`/`code`). That set appears only in an example config, not in any contract.

The naming example it cites, `210-review.code.github-copilot-vs-code-ide-support.md`, is a legacy artifact that likely predates the contract. Under the default `review_unknown_as = "fail"`, every pre-contract review would block. Tests should include real artifacts in the production format, per the parsing rules in project settings.

findings.title: The design carries unused scope: cut or defer it
findings.description:
The stated need is: when a slice's tasks are done, route to a review instead of advancing, and block on a failing verdict. The design adds well beyond that:
- `pre-slice-plan` is defined in the config schema but its logic is deferred, so it is schema nothing uses yet. Also drop the fourth Anticipated Slice from this initiative.
- Verdict handling reads and stores `score` and has a "documented code path" for enforcement. It also carries `criteria` and `provenance` as opaque fields with "no v1 consumer".
- `review_unknown_as` adds a policy knob that multiplies the test matrix. The default of treating UNKNOWN as FAIL could be hardcoded in v1.
- Per-gate `threshold` overrides sit on top of the global threshold, on top of `review_enabled`, with `reviewType` only configurable per gate.

Suggested v1: a `pre-advance` gate only, one `reviewType` key, one threshold key, and UNKNOWN = FAIL. Reading only `verdict` avoids the nested-table problem entirely. Add per-gate overrides when a second gate actually exists.

findings.title: Priority renumbering rationale is inaccurate
findings.description: The document says a branch between 5 and 6 "requires renumbering to avoid fractional priorities". `getNext()` already has a `Priority 2.5` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:187`). The proposed full renumber, or conversion to named stages, creates diff churn unrelated to the gate. Use a named comment such as `Gate: pre-advance review` instead and leave the others.
